why: riṇaté (√ri, 'release') fits 'āpo riṇate vanāni' and the accented-verb pattern of the yát clause; gṛṇate would make no sense here.
mítrāvaruṇā is pāda-initial (after the 12-syllable first pāda), so the vocative carries udatta on its first syllable; marks are consistent.
pṛṇaté 'to the generous one' pairs naturally with yájvane; grammar and accent are regular.
Both anudattas of prathamó are marked because the word opens the half-verse after the danda, the edition's usual line-start marking.
váreṇa 'by (his) choice' is a regular form and the accents (udatta va, svarita re) are consistent; vájreṇa does not fit Vaiśvānara.
stávamāna 'being praised' is a regular participle of stu with the expected accent; sense and metre are fine.
daśamáṃ návam 'the tenth, new (praise)' is coherent; nothing wrong.
pṛthivyā́ ayám 'this (Agni) is lord of earth' is grammatical and the accents are consistent; vayám would break the sense.
aritéva nā́vam 'like a rower the boat' is the intended simile; nā́vam is correct.
pávamānena is the instrumental agreeing with tváyā; regular.
āpiré is the perfect middle of √āp ('the inspired ones attained'); regular form and accent.
vakṣayam (aorist causative, 'I made grow') is a regular unaccented main-clause verb at pāda end.
yūyám 'you (pl.)' is the subject of ádadāta; correct.
vareyám (wooing) with final udatta is a regular form; sense of the wedding hymn line is fine.
váreṇa with udatta on va and svarita on re is consistent after sahasānó; váruṇa would not fit the sense.
víśvéd u (viśvā + íd + u) has two udattas and u is sannatara before tā́, which is exactly what the marks show.

suggest: विश्वे॑भिः सो॒म्यं मध्व॑ग्न॒ इन्द्रे॑ण वा॒युना॑ । पिबा॑ मि॒त्रस्य॒ धाम॑भिः ॥
why: mádhu has udatta on ma, so the following syllable dhvag must carry the svarita mark (as ऽग्ने॑ does in the next verse); the typed line omits it.

why: The pāda opens with a svarita-marked syllable (impossible without a preceding udatta) and has only 10 syllables for triṣṭubh; the accented preverb प्र is missing at the start.
vṛṣabhám opens the verse, so both anudattas before the udatta are marked, as in सु॒शि॒ल्पे and अ॒नृ॒क्ष॒रा elsewhere in this edition.
ví yád vā́cam has three consecutive udattas and the svarita on caṃ is correctly placed; yád vā would be a different, wrong reading.
devátā ṛ́ṣiḥ with hiatus and sannatara ta before ṛ́ is consistent; this is a reading, not a typo.
krátuṃ raghúm 'a light mind' is the sense of the line; raghúm is correct, rayím would not fit.
kṣaítrāya sā́dhase 'for success in the field' is grammatical; rā́dhase is not required.
pávamānena súṣṭutāḥ 'praised by Pavamāna' is a regular instrumental.
bā́dhase śátrūn 'you repel enemies' is the sense; bā́dhase is correct.

vidháveva devaráṃ 'as a widow her brother-in-law' is the intended simile.

aśvínā + ā́ (preverb of vavṛtyāḥ) merge to aśvínā́ with two udattas, so the svarita falling on va is correct.
yád vā́jām̐ abhy ádravas 'when you ran toward the prizes' is grammatical with candrabindu sandhi; fine.
víśve devāso is the vocative plural echoed in the next line; correct.
tritáṃ járāya jurátām 'let old age wear down Trita' is coherent; jánāya would not fit jurátām.
mádhunā 'with honey' is the natural complement of pṛṅktám havī́ṃṣi.
ródasyoḥ is the regular genitive-locative dual of ródasī; correct.
yád dhárī is yád + hárī with regular sandhi; the accent marks match.
suvṛ́tā 'well-rolling' describes the chariot alongside trivṛ́tā; correct.
sujātā́ 'well-born' (vocative dual with narā) is regular.

vā́ryasya dātrásya 'of the desirable gift' is coherent; sū́ryasya would not fit.

jīráyaḥ 'the swift ones' (subject of sisrate) is a regular form.
vanvaté 'to the conqueror' fits the list of datives in this verse.
rápasaḥ yuyodhi 'ward off injuries' is the sense; rápasaḥ is correct.
suvitā́ 'good fortune' parallels sumnā́ and saúbhagā in the same verse; savitā́ would not fit.
ūrmáyaḥ pavanta 'the waves purify' is the subject; correct.
śrutám 'the famed one' is the object of anūṣata; the missing space before the danda matches the previous verse in this edition.
nahí vām ásti dūraké 'it is not far for you' is grammatical.
pṛthivyā́ḥ opens the half-verse, so both leading anudattas are marked per the edition's convention.
éty ékaḥ (eti + ekaḥ) with sandhi and two udattas is regular.
